rationale: This is the archive's WorkingCapitalTurnoverValue with a 3-year moving average and a 1% winsor bolted on — a measurement-robustness tweak to an already jointly significant signal rather than a substantively different construct, and it burns a slot on a variant whose result will be nearly collinear with the parent.

The level-versus-change decomposition of the velocity channel is a legitimate and non-cosmetic question and the expression matches the hypothesis, but change-in-turnover interacted with book-to-market sits very close to the Piotroski F-score's ΔATO component applied to value stocks, so novelty is limited and the result should be interpreted against that benchmark.

The algebra is internally consistent (cash enters once net of non-cash current assets) and a signed price-scaled variable is the right way to reconcile the archive's conflicting FMB and alpha evidence, but the construct is effectively a fixed-weight linear combination of two already-tested legs and overlaps the documented cash-to-price / net-liquid-assets-to-price literature, so the informational upside is mostly diagnostic.

Adding a second-moment test to the one channel that actually produced joint evidence is a coherent next step and the sign convention is correct, but the proposal is internally inconsistent with its own companion signal — it leaves the act−che denominator unwinsorized inside VOL, exactly the defect Signal 1 claims to repair, so the volatility term will be outlier-driven for cash-heavy firms.

The two legs are mechanically linked — a high cash share of current assets shrinks the act−che denominator and thus inflates sale/(act−che) — so the signal cannot cleanly test the claimed complementarity, and one leg (cash share) already had a wrong-signed FMB slope, making a simple rank-sum composite likely to blur rather than resolve the archive's FMB/alpha conflict.

The expression is algebraically just 1 − NOWC/(act−che), i.e. another scaling of the already-tested soft-capital quantity, but the operating-liability-leverage framing (Nissim–Penman) gives it a genuinely different and testable sign prediction from the archive's liability-growth distress signal, so it is a defensible if incremental use of a slot.
